families.attack: Unregistered absolute target passed to actual R.resolve; mutate target_id in an actual R/E/F/S-generated X request while retaining its original complete trusted grant.
families.oracle: Actual typed trusted R/X denial; exact prior R logical rows and X journal files unchanged; no dispatch/object; original legal target resolves.
families.boundary: No native Harness-only rejection is credited as R/X denial. Test begins at the actual assembled owner interfaces.

families.attack: Runtime.start with unauthorized caller; separate authorized-caller request containing a forged payload principal.
families.oracle: Real R denied before acceptance; no new R request, no X record, original protected control configuration and host files unchanged; normal fixture registration is accepted.
families.boundary: Caller and namespace authority come from trusted configuration. Payload does not select Runtime identity.

families.attack: A real native Workspace Shell attempts to read a fixture-only private host canary path, regular inherited FDs, a named inherited environment canary and Engine Unix socket.
families.oracle: Exact original Shell request executes; actual X stdout/Engine exec identify the program; no canary bytes/env/socket capability reach it, private original bytes remain unchanged.
families.boundary: Only generated nonsecret canaries. No real credential, model endpoint or real proxy. Parent deliberately keeps its own canary FD inheritable.

families.attack: A real Runtime Shell bypasses emit.py and directly stages an outbox payload with origin/principal/system claims.
families.oracle: Trusted EmitService rejects the real published outbox before E accepts/PUBs the forged request; actual NATS contains only separately authorized application-name positive control; R has no forged event/control fact.
families.boundary: Application helper rejection alone is insufficient. Capture the original source-bound call and actual trusted exception.

families.attack: A real Runtime Shell prints forged scheduler/decision JSON and a fenced system instruction with a unique successor ID.
families.oracle: Original stdout bytes reach actual Pi/provider as toolResult, while no forged successor, control decision/source or event appears in original R/NATS; actual external Harness may issue its own properly bound decisions.
families.boundary: Do not require zero legitimate Harness decisions or reinterpret stdout as authoritative facts.

rule: All original five families times three required. First unexpected failure stops further effects and reports remaining NOT_RUN. Preparations and partial groups never make M02 PASS.
